content.summary: At 9AM last Thursday, everything seemed normal. Microsoft employees were arriving on campus, ready for a regular day of emails and meetings. But barely an hour later, one of Microsoft's worst outages in history started to unfold, leaving employees, businesses, and many governments without access to Outlook emails for nearly 24 hours. It all started in Switzerland, according to a source familiar with the outage. Exchange Online servers that power Outlook started to fall offline. The problem quickly spread to Mexico, and then to other countries around the world, as Microsoft's failover systems tried to shift email traffic elsewhere.
